text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
KING HENRY II, the first Plantagenet King of England, was born in 1133.
Irish zoologist RICHARD MINCHIN, the first Director of the Adelaide Zoo, was born on this day in 1831.

Well-known South Australian physician SIR CONSTANTINE TRENT CHAMPION DE CRESPIGNY, was born in 1882. He had a challenging outlook : "When in doubt, do the most difficult thing". Debonair British actor REX (REGINALD CARY) HARRISON ("MY FAIR LADY", "THE GHOST AND MRS MUIR", "DOCTOR DOOLITTLE") who starred in more than 40 films, was born in 1908. He died in 1990.
Australian jockey 'DARBY' MUNRO, who won his first Melbourne Cup on "Peter Pan" in 1934, was born in 1913.
Australian classical musician and conductor BARRY TUCKWELL was born in 1931.
British musicial star ELAINE PAGE, who shot to stardom in "EVITA"and "CATS", was born in 1952.

British/Australian singer ANDY GIBB was born in 1958. He was the younger brother of the GIBB brothers who formed the successful 'Bee Gees'. Between 1977 and 1981 his solo career was also successful with hits such as "I Just Wanna Be Your Everything" (1977), "Love Is Thicker Than Water" (1977) and "Shadow Dancing" (1978). In 1983 he played one of the main roles in "Joseph And The Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat". While in Britain in March 1988 he died in an Oxford hospital. The official cause of death was heart failure. He had just signed a new recording contract with Island.
** EVENTS **
1461 : HENRY VI of England was deposed by the Duke of
York, during the War of the Roses.
1770 : British troops opened fire on a rowdy crowd in
Boston, Massachusetts, killing 5 Americans. The incident became known as the "BOSTON MASSACRE". No text received
1778 : British composer THOMAS ARNE, who wrote more than
50 operas and whose work included "Rule Britannia", died.
1790 : FLORA MacDONALD, Scottish Jacobite heroine, died.
In 1746 she helped Bonnie Prince CHARLIE, the Stuart claimant to the British throne, escape from the Hebridean island of Benbecula.
1803 : Australia's first newspaper, the SYDNEY GAZETTE

AND NEW SOUTH WALES ADVERTISER, was published. The first 6 issues (consisting of 4 pages printed badly on foolscap paper), came out on Saturdays, but this was changed to Sundays, and the paper survived for almost 7 years.
1912 : Is this where it started? In Kalgoorlie the
Australian Natives Association gave notice of a resolution calling for Australia to be a republic.
1918 : Moscow was declared the new Russian capital to
replace Petrograd. Two days later the Bolsheviks changed their name to the Russian Communist Party.
1922 : In the United States ANNIE OAKLEY shot a record 98
out of a hundred clay targets.
1930 : American food scientist CLARENCE BIRDSEYE
developed the quick-freeze technique, claiming to have revolutionised the way food is stored. His frozen fish had been on the American market since 1925.
1933 : Election returns in Germany gave the Nazis and
their allies 52 percent of seats in the Reichstag.
1936 : The British VICKERS aircraft company unveiled its
new fighter plane, the Supermarine Spitfire. It was designed by REGINALD MITCHELL, who drew up the plans after spending many hours watching how seagulls flew.
1945 : Two of Australia's best known Generals and nine

other military staff were killed when their plane crashed into the sea north of Cairns. Major-General GEORGE VASEY and Major-General RUPERT DOWNES were heading for New Guinea. VASEY was Australia's top divisional commander in the Kokoda campaign.
1946 : British Prime Minister WINSTON CHURCHILL coined
the phrase "Iron Curtain", when referring to the threat posed to Europe by Russia.
1953 : Soviet leader JOSEPH STALIN died of a brain haemorrhage. He was seen as the country's saviour after breaking HITLER's military power at Stalingrad during World War Two.
1966 : The criminal overlords of London's East End,
RONALD and REGINALD KRAY, were jailed for 30 years for murder.
1966 : 124 people were killed when a British airliner
slammed into Mount Fuji in Japan.
1982 : One of the Blues Brothers, JOHN BELUSHI, died of a
drug overdose. The US singer, film actor and comedian fostered a cult following.
1983 : BOB HAWKE led the Labor Party to power, defeating
the Liberal government of MALCOLM FRASER.
1984 : Scientists warned of the dangers of the

"greenhouse effect". University of East Anglia researchers claimed the increased production of carbon dioxide was heating up the earth's atmosphere. They warned that a warmer climate could harm agriculture and cause flooding by melting the polar ice caps.
1991 : Iraq gave up its claim to Kuwait, and freed the
last of its allied prisoners, taken during the Gulf War.
